lesson.title: Condition Loops
lesson.driving_question: How can a program keep asking until a condition changes?
lesson.primary_concept_family: A while loop repeats while its condition remains True, and a counter can bound the repetitions.
misconceptions: A while loop checks its condition before each repetition.
The loop must change a value used by its condition.
The counter update belongs inside the loop.
A bounded loop can stop even when the target has not been reached.

progression.make: build a bounded password retry loop

code_expectations: Use a condition that can change.
Test both early success and the limit.

shared_program.code:
target = 7
attempts = 0
guess = 0
while guess != target and attempts < 3:
    guess = int(input("Guess 1 to 10: " ))
    attempts = attempts + 1
print("Finished in", attempts, "tries.")

questions: Which two stored values change each time the loop runs?
Why does the terminating guess still increase the attempt counter?
If the guesses are 2 and then 7, what does the final line display?
Why does the loop stop after three wrong guesses even though the target was not found?

primm.prompt: Reduce the limit to two attempts. Test one run by guessing 7 first and another with two wrong guesses. The program must report 1 try and 2 tries.
Give the player five attempts. Update the finishing message to report the guesses used. Test an early correct guess and five unsuccessful guesses; both counts must be accurate.

Store "open" in [password]. Use a while loop to ask for a door code until the user enters "open" or [attempts] reaches 3. Add 1 to [attempts] after each answer. Test "open"; display "Door opened. Attempts used: 1". Test "red", "blue" and "green"; display "Door locked. Attempts used: 3".
Repair the counter update so the loop can reach its limit. Test a successful guess and three failed guesses.

blocks.definition: A while loop repeats an indented block while its condition is True. The condition is checked before each repetition.
A loop condition must be able to change. Here, guess changes when the user enters a new value.
A counter records how many times a loop has run. Start it before the loop and update it inside the loop.
A bounded loop has a limit, so it will stop after a known number of attempts even if the target is not reached.
A stopping rule describes when repetition ends. A while loop stops when its condition becomes False.
